name: Hand-drawn annotation callouts

source.description: Three inspected references add margin notes: handwritten labels with arrows and loops pointing at what to notice.

technique: A note in a handwritten or italic voice, a loop around the subject and a curved arrow between them name the thing the viewer should notice, like a teacher marking up a page. The hand-made marks contrast with clean geometry, so they read as commentary rather than content.
purpose: Direct attention; explain a mechanism in place; add a human voice to technical material.
visual_behaviour: A loop is drawn around a target, an arrow curves from a short note to it, the note pops in with a slight tilt; marks fade when the point is made.
mechanics: Stroke-draw of an overshooting hand loop (0.5 s), arrow shaft (0.35 s) and head (0.15 s); note pop with back ease; positions from the target's rendered box.

decomposition.timing: About 0.6-0.9 s to complete; held 1.5-4 s.

parameters.name: loop
parameters.description: Draw a loop around the target

failure_modes: Notes over moving targets drift off (measure once; keep the target still)
More than two notes at once clutters
Handwritten fonts outside the HyperFrames-bundled set need @font-face

implementation.approach: Studio.comp.callout: Studio.boxAt on the target, Studio.draw.loop + quadratic arrow drawn with Studio.draw.stroke, note popped with Studio.space.pop, clamped to the safe area.

measurements.value: 50.8 ms/frame median, peak headless Chromium 255 MB

provenance.observed: Handwritten notes with arrows label a bouncing ball and an easing curve.
A hand-drawn oval circles duplicated messages with a short label.
A small parenthetical aside sits beside a word as a spoken-voice comment.

evidence.notes: Contact sheet inspected: loop, arrow and note around the hand-off zone.
Two margin notes placed per format (two lines in portrait and square to clear the sheet and HUD) and a note on the flight's landing dot. Frame review 0 errors, 0 warnings (preview grade).

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown). Notes and drawings are original.
